question: State the conditions that a registered person must satisfy to take input tax credit under section 16 of the CGST Act, 2017, and the time limit for taking it.
sources: CGST Act, 2017 - section 16 eligibility and conditions for taking input tax credit

points.label: Eligibility
points.description: A registered person may take credit of tax charged on goods or services used or intended to be used in the course or furtherance of business.

points.label: Tax invoice and supplier's details
points.description: He must hold a tax invoice or debit note, and the supplier must have reported the invoice in his outward supply statement so that it is communicated to the recipient.

points.label: Receipt of goods or services
points.description: He must have received the goods or services; goods delivered to another person on his direction count as received. Where goods come in lots, credit is taken on receipt of the last lot.
points.basis: CGST Act, 2017, section 16(2)(b) and first proviso

points.label: Tax paid and return filed
points.description: The tax charged must actually have been paid to the Government by the supplier, and the recipient must have filed his return under section 39.

points.label: Payment to supplier within 180 days
points.description: If the recipient does not pay the supplier the value and tax within 180 days of the invoice, the credit taken is added back to his output tax liability with interest; it can be taken again after payment.
points.basis: CGST Act, 2017, second and third provisos to section 16(2)

points.label: Time limit and depreciation
points.description: Credit cannot be taken after 30 November following the end of the financial year of the invoice, or the filing of the annual return, whichever is earlier; no credit is allowed on the tax component on which depreciation is claimed.
